metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Lazy Market Companion
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Auto-lists your always-sell items and matches market board prices
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Keep an Auto-Market list of items you always sell. The companion lists them through your retainers in the stack size you choose (keeping a reserve in your bags if you want), prices every listing by matching the lowest board price instead of undercutting, and can do all of it inside AutoRetainer's venture cycle. Also re-prices existing listings (Auto Pinch). Successor to Dagobert Price Matcher; your old settings are imported automatically.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.15 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.
- Untried build: tested offline against a saved-configuration round trip (the plugin's offline test suite), not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.13 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's confirmation dialogs open now.** In 0.2.8.12, "Add all visible", "Remove all visible" and the panel's Enable Auto-Market switch each tried to show a confirmation dialog under a different name than the one they opened it with, so no dialog could ever appear and those controls did nothing when clicked. The names now match, and a regression test scans the panel's code so a button and its dialog cannot drift apart silently again.
- Correction to 0.2.8.12's notes: the panel's Enable Auto-Market switch asks for confirmation before turning Auto-Market on. That confirmation is the panel's own safety - the main window's switch has never had one, and 0.2.8.12's notes wrongly implied it did.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.12 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **A new Auto-Market panel window lists every marketable stack in your bags and whether it is on the Auto-Market list** - the same two states the bag dots mark (plus what a dot cannot show: entries whose tick is unticked, and the quick-exclude flag), as a table with quantities. Each row has quick Add/Remove, and entries expose the same stack-size, keep-in-bags and skip-routing edits as the main window's table. The panel covers your four bag containers, which is what Auto-Market's bags stock source draws from.
- **"Add all visible" / "Remove all visible" add or remove exactly the rows the filters currently show**, with the count on the button and a confirmation dialog before anything changes.
- **The panel carries the global Auto-Market knobs** in a collapsible section: master switch, markers, AutoRetainer, stock source, pricing, reserve slots, pinch behaviour, listing order, the value gate and auto-assign - the same controls as the Auto-Market tab, writing the same settings. What the main window does not expose is not exposed here either. The master switch keeps its confirmation on turning on and stays locked while a run is in progress.
- **Status filters, a name search, a category filter, and an optional count of unmarketable stacks** (hidden by default, like the dots' "no dot at all"). On-list rows keep the list's own order; everything else sorts by name. The panel never fetches prices, so the price-based listing orders are not applied here.
- **The panel docks beside the inventory window**: to its right when the screen has room, else to its left, else it floats at a position it remembers (clamped on screen, so it can never drift out of reach). It opens with the inventory, closes with it unless pinned, and `/lmc panel` toggles it any time. An inventory window that cannot be read is just the floating case - the panel always appears, and the plugin log's open line carries the dock mode, position, size, the inventory rectangle and scale it read, and the row counts.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.11 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Auto-Market marker dots are now drawn through a single full-screen drawing layer instead of one window per dot.** Every dot is painted directly onto one transparent overlay that covers the game's window - the same drawing path other screens in this plugin family use for game-anchored overlays - at exactly the same position as before. One window per dot could report itself healthy while nothing appeared on screen; that layer is gone entirely.
- **The markers log now checks each drawn dot against the inventory window's own position.** The game reports where the inventory window itself is (position, size, scale) in the same frame the dots are drawn; every measured dot is graded on-addon or OFF-ADDON against it, with its offset from the window's corner, so a placement mismatch names itself.
- **The markers log now reports the drawing viewport beside the game window's size** (window size, viewport size, display scale factor), so a scaled or letterboxed buffer shows up as two different sizes for the same screen.
- **`/lmc markertest` is now an A/B pair across the old and new drawing paths.** Dot A is drawn through the new single-overlay path every marker uses; dot B through the old one-window-per-dot path. A visible without B means the old per-dot windows were the problem; both means the drawing works; neither means something outside the marker layer blocks the overlay too.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: LazyCrafter
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: What can I make right now, what's it worth, and what would it take to make the rest?
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Catalogs every recipe you can craft, buckets them by how much effort the missing materials take, prices them with Universalis, and hands the missing-material work to Artisan / GBR / ARC / Lifestream.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.7.9 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.
- If Knightshopper is missing, busy, refuses LazyCrafter, or has no unlocked vendor for an item, those items fall back to the usual shopping stops - flagged and named in chat exactly as before. Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

v0.1.7.6 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the catalog and price settings (recipes above the character's level, the undersupplied thresholds, the revenue basis, pricing at the home world only, the price refresh interval, the price-match message) and the cart-run hand-off switches (fetching materials from retainers, walking to a summoning bell or to vendors, preferring a currency shop) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.7.5 (2026-09-16)

- **The shopping-stop Resume popup window is gone.** The 0.1.7.4 test pass: the full-screen popup opened at every shopping stop sat over the game and blocked mouse input with the client - verdict: remove the resume extra window. The window is removed and nothing else changed: a blocked shopping stop still says the what-to-do message in chat and on the Run tab exactly once, and Resume stays on the Run tab button, in chat (/lcraft resume) and the copied report - keyboard-only resume works

v0.1.7.4 (2026-09-15)

- **The retainer batch fetch no longer calls every session a zero-move without counting the bags.** The 0.1.6.16 early exit for an instantly-dead bell session sat ABOVE the bag-delta measurement with the moved counter still 0 from wave start, so every batch session ended as "the retainer fetch moved nothing into the bags", the cart held for Resume, and the per-item fallback never ran - the 0.1.7.3 test runs show exactly this shape (batch queued, retainers scanned, 0 counted). The exit now runs AFTER the measurement: a genuinely empty session still stops with the bell named, a session that moved anything trims the remainder into the per-item pass

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Akari
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Market Helper
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Undercut, list, gather and buy — market board automation end to end.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Market Helper is an all-in-one market board tool with five tabs:

UNDERCUT — Walk a summoning bell's retainers and undercut every listed item. HQ and NQ are handled separately, your own retainers are matched rather than undercut, per-item overrides and price memory are supported, an obvious troll price is skipped, and mannequin/display items are never touched (if a row can't be verified it is skipped rather than risk delisting it). Closes the bell when it finishes.

LISTER — Build a list (hold CTRL and hover an item, or search) and press Go to list them all. Prices each item at the most common market price, ignoring lone troll listings, against your world, data center or whole region. Per-item stack sizes and list amounts, rolls extra items to the next retainer at the 20-slot cap, and includes a no-touch dry run.

FLIPPER — Compare any marketable item across Japan, America, Europe and Materia via Universalis. Top 10 listings per region, best cross-region flip, and seller/buyer tax modelling.

ITEM GATHERER — Pull designated items off your retainers into your bags, optionally returning your market listings first. Manual withdraw/deposit actions included.

BUYER — Build a shopping list by hand or import a MakePlace furniture list, then SCAN the market per world via Universalis and press SEND to travel with Lifestream and buy across worlds. Every purchase is verified against the game's own confirmation dialog before it is accepted. Listings are bought whole, so by default it never buys a bigger stack than you still need, and a hard sanity ceiling caps the price even with no cap set. If a planned listing has already been bought it chases the next cheapest, on other worlds if needed, until your order is filled. Dry run is on by default.

Open with /markethelp, /market, /mh, or /undercut.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: yagi2
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Restocker
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Bulk reprice and split-list retainer market listings across all retainers.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Cross-retainer market workbench with a plan-then-apply flow. Reprice tab: per-retainer 'lowest -N g' / 'lowest exact' buttons walk each listing, fetch live market data via Dalamud's IMarketBoard.OfferingsReceived (skipping your own retainers, deduplicated per item/HQ), stage every change in a queue, then commit them all via a single Apply that calls SetRetainerMarketPrice directly. New listing tab: per-row qty x slots, target retainer combo, auto stack-splitting (e.g. 990 / 99 → ten listings of 99), and direct listing from character bag / Chocobo Saddlebag with no entrust step (saddle items are bulk-staged to the bag in one phase, then listed). Live progress dialog shows the current step (selecting retainer, fetching market data, listing, …) so long runs don't look frozen. Six-language UI (EN/JA/DE/FR/ZH/KO). Warns once at startup if AutoRetainer is also loaded since both drive retainer summoning.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog: 0.1.0.0 — Initial release.

v1.0.8: Added /acplugin command for consistent access alongside /ac legacy alias.
v1.0.7: UI redesign ? removed Auto-Discard toggle; separate Move To Inventory and Discard All buttons; both now use random 800-1100ms delays for consistent pacing; direct discard from armoury is now the default for Discard All.
v1.0.6: Direct discard from armoury ? new option (under Auto-Discard) skips the move-to-inventory step and discards items straight from the armoury slot, with automatic fallback to move+discard if the game rejects it.
v1.0.5: Internal cleanup; repo renamed to AschyQOL.
v1.0.4: Discard All uses random 800-1100ms delay between items; Cancel Queue button.
v1.0.3: Auto-Discard mode via InventoryManager.DiscardItem.
v1.0.0: Initial release.

metadataCompletePlugins.description:

Open the Recruitment Criteria form (Recruit Members) to save or apply. Use /clarion.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: XivHub
metadataCompletePlugins.name: InventoryCleaner
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Keep only the gear you actually use.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Tidies the Armoury Chest against your saved gearsets. Anything equipped, referenced by a gearset, or a higher-ilvl upgrade for a job you still play is kept; everything else is moved out to your bags, fullest armoury container first, so the run frees space where it is tightest. Every run is previewed item by item with the reason for each decision, and nothing moves until you confirm.

Also does the reverse (pulling gearset pieces back into the armoury) and offers a discard picker: an icon grid of leftover gear, framed by rarity, where anything equipped, in a gearset, or on your allowlist is never listed.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Lazy Hub
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: One window for every lalalazy plugin.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: One in-game window for the whole lalalazy suite. Turn plugins on and off, change their common settings and open their windows from one place, with Gluttony Combo's Auto-Rotation switch and drag-to-hotbar action buttons up front, plus a server info bar entry. Open it with /lazy.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.1.0 (2026-10-03) [testing]

- **Switches and settings for the whole suite.** Plugins that offer controls can be turned on or off and have their common settings changed from the hub, over Dalamud IPC. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the owning plugin's own window does; the hub never writes another plugin's configuration.
- **Quick tab:** a Gluttony Combo tray with the Auto-Rotation switch and hotbar buttons (click a button, then click a hotbar slot to place the action; Escape cancels), then one switch per plugin that offers one. Switches with real consequences (Auto-Market, the FATE bot) ask for a second click within a few seconds.
- **Plugin page:** the plugin's settings in groups: switches, number steppers (`-` and `+`) and option pickers (`<` and `>`). A setting that another plugin or a running task holds is shown as locked with the reason and refuses changes.
- **Plugins tab:** all fifteen plugins with status, Settings and Open. A plugin on a version that does not offer controls yet has Open only.
- **Safe mode:** `/lazy safe` switches to the plain window and back. The choice is remembered.
- **Look:** the window frame is tinted toward lalalazy green with forest-green panels, gold accents and each plugin's icon.

- **Plugin icons fit their slot.** They were drawn at their full 64-pixel size instead of the 44-pixel slot, which covered the first letters of each name and status line and touched the row below.

- Testing channel only. Plugins offer controls from the versions released with this one: update them to see their settings here.
- The hub asks each plugin for its controls about once a second while the window is open and not at all while it is closed.
- After an update the "What's new" window shows these notes once. `/lazy changelog` reopens them.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-10-03)

- **First release: one in-game window for the whole lalalazy suite.** `/lazy` (or `/lazyhub`) opens a native game-style window with two tabs.
- **Plugins tab:** all fifteen lalalazy plugins in a grid, each with its icon, its name, a live status and an Open button. Status reads as Loaded, Loaded (testing), Not loaded or Not installed, and refreshes about once a second. Open launches that plugin's main window (or its settings window when it has no main window) and is available only while the plugin is running.
- **Quick tab:** shows whether Gluttony Combo's auto-rotation is on or off, read from Gluttony Combo itself. The card says so when Gluttony Combo is not running.
- **Server info bar entry** showing how many of the suite's plugins are running, for example `13/15`. Clicking it opens or closes the window.
- The plugin opens from the Dalamud plugin installer's Open button as well.

- This is a testing-channel first release. It reads status and opens windows; it does not change any plugin's settings yet.
- The window uses the stock game window frame. The icons are the repository's pixel-art plugin icons.
- After an update the "What's new" window shows these notes once. `/lazy changelog` reopens them.

metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Track your Skyward points for all jobs toward the Pteranodon mount
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Tracks all jobs' Skyward points for the Pteranodon mount achievement. Scans your inventory for Skybuilders turn-in items and projects how many points they'll add, shown as a cyan bar extension on each job's progress bar. Use /lazysky to open.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.0.3.1 (2026-10-04) [testing]

- Fixed a rare game crash when the plugin updates while the game is running: while the achievement-progress hook is active and the plugin is updated again, it is disabled only after any call still inside it has finished, so a call can no longer land on a hook that is already gone. Skybuilders' point tracking is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: yocopk
metadataCompletePlugins.name: MogHouse Companion
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Quality-of-life tools that connect your game to MogHouse. Timers and duty pops, pushed to your phone.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Companion plugin for MogHouse (mog-house.com).

An all-in-one home for quality-of-life tools that link FINAL FANTASY XIV to your MogHouse account. Tools are added over time; each one can be switched on or off individually, and nothing leaves the game unless you enable it.

Timers: reads the timers you already see in the game's own Timers window (CTRL+U), including submarine and airship voyages, retainer ventures, map and leve allowances, custom deliveries and allied society dailies, and syncs them to your profile. MogHouse then pushes you a notification the moment one comes up, on web and mobile, even while the game and your PC are off. Voyages are timed to the last vessel back, so one notification means the whole fleet is home.

Duty Finder: when the confirm window appears, MogHouse pushes the duty or roulette name to your phone, so you know whether it is worth the sprint back to the desk. By default it stays quiet while the game is the window you are looking at.

The plugin is read-only: it collects your own data and reports status. It never performs an in-game action — it will not commence a duty for you, and it does not skip, confirm or automate anything.

Open it with /moghouse. Requires a MogHouse account, and a free one is enough: it syncs one character and sends one timer alert of your choosing, plus duty pops. Mog+ lifts both limits and warns you before a timer lands rather than as it does.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: nxships
metadataCompletePlugins.name: PlayerNexusTracker
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Track every adventurer you meet in Eorzea.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Track players you meet in FFXIV — who they are, when you ran into them, how their characters change over time. A focused social tracker built on the NexusKit framework.

Per-player detail view with Summary, Equipment, Class/Jobs, Achievements, Free Company, Encounters, History and Notes tabs. Optional enrichment from Lodestone (gear, FC link, achievement progress) and FFXIVCollect (mounts, minions, full achievement catalog). Live throttled refresh queue keeps external data fresh without hammering either service.

Configurable chat and toast notifications when players you've seen before change — rename, server transfer, Free Company join/leave/switch, achievement growth, refresh failures. Per-event filtering and history grouping so the chat doesn't drown you.

Powerful player-filter language with live preview to slice your list however you want; encounter history scoped per duty and content type; optional bridges to other Dalamud plugins (Lifestream world-travel, more to come).

Local-first: all data lives in a single SQLite file under your XIVLauncher config. Automated weekly maintenance keeps it tidy. English and German localization.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: VimaFFXIV
metadataCompletePlugins.name: SharkChat
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Auto-replace words in your outgoing chat messages.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
SharkChat intercepts your chat before it's sent and swaps words or phrases for whatever you want.

Set up rules like Thanks → Thankies, and they'll apply automatically every time you chat — across any channel.

Features:
• Whole-word matching (so "tank" won't mangle "thanks")
• Case-insensitive by default
• Per-rule enable/disable
• Live preview so you can test rules before using them

Commands:
/shark — toggle on/off
/shark config — open settings

metadataCompletePlugins.author: The Redheaded Witch, WillWolf76
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Fashion Report Calculator / Dye Finder
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Know your Fashion Report points on the spot and help crowdsource new items and dyes!
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
This is the new and improved Fashion Report System. This plugin will allow you to open a window that will show you what your fashion report status is vs the current week's theme.

There are a few parts to this. Since the only way to get Fashion Report for the week to my knowledge is speaking to Masked Rose after Tuesdays reset, this plugin takes the first person who does talk to him and updates everyone else. So only one person per week needs to speak to Masked Rose.

You can click on a theme and pull all the known items for that theme for that specific slot. You also get a very detailed breakdown of how much points you are getting based on what you are currently wearing.

The plugin also stores the attempts of those using the mod (just the data from fashioncheck, no user information) so that we can figure out the dyes faster and share information faster. The information in this table is wiped every week since once we discover the dyes, it is useless.

I still have more upgrades to do, including adding a dye window and the window that will help calculate the weekly dyes. I already have an idea of how I want to write them, so it shouldn't take me too long. If you have suggestions on how I can upgrade this, please share with me on github!

Credit for the program goes to it's original creator, WillWolf76, who wrote this for me originally.

When this plugin updates the database, it also updates my Discord Bot which you can set up to post fashion report each week. It's set to update on Tuesdays and Fridays (week start and dye information added). Link to add the Discord Bot is in the about section.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog: Fixed some minor bugs.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Lazy Gear Collector
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Track upgradable gear sets and what it costs to finish them
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Tracks upgradable gear collections piece by piece. Starts with Occult Crescent: North Horn's Phantom Vision sets - all 7 roles, 5 slots, 4 tiers. Shows which pieces you own and at what tier, what the next upgrade costs, and the exact obol/fixative shortfall to finish a role or the whole collection. Every item ID and price is read from the game's own shop data at runtime, so it stays correct across patches. Also flags Arcanaut's gear you can trade up for free. Use /lazygear to open.

- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers whether the saddlebag and retainers count and the target tier to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.0.2.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After Lazy Gear Collector updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read. Type `/lazygear changelog` any time to reopen it.
- No change to collection tracking: the Phantom Vision set, tier detection, ownership counting and the remaining-cost figures are all unchanged.

v0.0.1.0 (2026-07-30)

- **First release.** Tracks upgradable gear collections: which pieces are owned, what tier each one
- **Phantom Vision (Occult Crescent: North Horn, patch 7.55)** as the first collection — 7 role sets
- **Runtime shop-derived pricing.** `ShopGraph.cs` builds a reverse index over the entire
- **Arcanaut's trade-up detection** (`Planner.DetectShortcut`). Arcanaut's +1 and +2 exchange into
- **Ownership scanning** across bags, armoury chest and equipped gear (live), plus opportunistic
- Role roster UI with click-through to per-piece detail, a wallet strip, per-role and

- **The glamour dresser cannot be enumerated** at Dalamud API level 15 — `MirageManager` exposes
- `ItemCostsStruct.CostType` is honoured when reading shop costs. `CostType == 0` means the cost
- Reference data behind this release, including the full item-ID matrix and the shop table, is in

- Release build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- The set-construction and pricing logic was re-implemented independently against a raw Lumina dump

Use /avf to open.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Armoire Auto-Fill
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Per-dungeon view of which armoire-eligible gear pieces you're still missing
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Lists every armoire-eligible dungeon drop in the game and shows whether each is in your inventory, in your armoire, or still missing. Sort by level, hide completed dungeons, toggle to show owned items too. Open the armoire UI at an inn once per session to populate the in-armoire state; in-inventory and equipped state is detected automatically.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.5.7.0 (2026-10-10)
- **The PvP shopping list now includes gear sold for Trophy Crystals and Wolf Collars.** The crystal quartermaster's Trophy Crystal Exchange (weapons, armour, accessories) and the collar quartermaster's exchange were missing from the list because their cost currencies were not mapped, so the PvP code came out empty. Both quartermasters are in the list now, checked against Knightshopper's own vendor catalog: every exported pair is one it accepts.
- Pieces no import code can name are now listed in the window by name with the reason (the shop has no vendor link in the game data, or Knightshopper has no vendor for its shop), instead of being dropped quietly. The Wolf Mark gear behind the mark quartermaster falls in this list: its shop opens through a dialogue handler, so no vendor pair can be written for it.
- The shopping summary line showed placeholder braces instead of the counts; it shows the numbers now.

v0.5.6.0 (2026-10-08)
- **Import codes now carry only what can actually be bought today.** Some pieces are gated behind more than a quest: seasonal vendors also gate pieces on an achievement, and the previous filter only knew about quests, so pieces the game would not sell yet were still written into the codes, and the first one of them made Knightshopper refuse the whole import ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"). The shopping list now checks live quest and achievement progress: what can be bought now goes into the code, a piece whose cheapest listing is locked falls back to a listing that can be bought, and a piece with no buyable listing at all is left out and counted at the bottom of the window ("N missing piece(s) need quest or achievement progress you don't have yet - left out of the import"). The rule applies to every currency, not just gil.

v0.5.5.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes now name vendors that Knightshopper itself has.** The previous build still produced Gil codes that Knightshopper refused whole ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"): the rule it used to decide which vendors Knightshopper knows was a guess and was wrong for most Gil shops. The rule now follows how Knightshopper builds its own vendor list: a vendor is an NPC the game actually places in an area, and seasonal NPCs that are re-used under new ids with the same name and the same shops count once. It applies to every currency, not just gil. The Gil code now carries several times as many pieces, because shops the old rule dropped by mistake are back.
- Placeholder items with no name are no longer put in a code; Knightshopper has no entry for them.
- Every code and every catalog entry was checked offline against the vendor data produced by Knightshopper's own library (not against this plugin's own model): no refusals. This is not yet confirmed in the game, and newer game patches than the one checked are not covered.
- The shopping-list section says what the codes were checked against and that it is not yet confirmed in-game; the copy message also explains that Knightshopper names only the first item it refuses.
- The vendor placement is read from the game's area files once per session in the background (about one second), with one log line.

v0.5.4.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes no longer contain items Knightshopper would refuse.** Knightshopper rejects a whole import when even one item is not in its own catalog, which the previous Gil code hit: shops whose vendors only spawn for an event never enter Knightshopper's catalog, but this plugin was still naming them. The catalog now only names shops with a permanently placed vendor, matching how Knightshopper derives its own list, and the same rule applies to every currency, not just gil.
- Pieces that this leaves out are no longer silent: the window shows "N items left out: Knightshopper cannot buy them", the build log counts the skipped shops, and the copy buttons never produce a code Knightshopper would answer with "not available from its shared vendor".

v0.5.3.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **The "Copy import code" instructions now name the exact controls.** After copying, the message says which currency window to open (the sidebar entry under "Currencies"), that the shopping-list dropdown sits at the top of the window next to "Buy All", and that the import is the clipboard icon labelled "Paste" at the right end of the "New list name..." row. It also names the list that will be created, quotes the confirmation line Knightshopper prints in chat ("Imported the shopping list from the clipboard."), and explains that each code only imports in its own currency's window - pasted elsewhere, Knightshopper refuses it and says which window to use.
- Currency names now match Knightshopper's own labels ("The Hunt" instead of "Hunt", "Tomestones" instead of "Tomestone", "Scrips" instead of "Scrip"), so the headings, the created list names and the instructions match what the sidebar shows.
- When Knightshopper is not loaded, the hint now points at the same controls instead of just saying "paste them".

v0.5.2.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **The shopping list now builds.** On the previous testing build the Knightshopper shopping list always showed "Shop catalog unavailable": one shop entry with an unusual data shape aborted the whole catalog. That entry is now skipped instead, the rest of the list still builds, and a failure is no longer retried every frame.
- The section now says what actually happened: game data not ready yet, a build failure (with a Refresh button — nothing retries automatically), or a normal empty result ("nothing to shop for").
- One line per build in the plugin log reports how many shops were scanned, skipped and failed, and how many entries each currency produced.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: XivHub
metadataCompletePlugins.name: AutoPincher
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: One-click retainer repricing against the live market board, fully local.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Repinches your retainer market listings by undercutting the cheapest live competitor by 1 gil. Reads each listing straight from game memory, clicks the in-game market board's Compare Prices to find the current cheapest offering, and sets your asking price to one below it, never below what a vendor gives, and never above your own cheapest copy. Your own retainers and housing mannequins are never treated as competitors, so two retainers selling the same item don't chase each other down. No server; nothing leaves your client unless you turn on the developer log and point it at your own server. Adds an Auto Pinch button next to AutoRetainer's retainer-list controls and a /autopinch command for the open retainer. AutoRetainer is optional (used only to pause its automation during a pinch run).

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: AutoPotion
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Per-job HP, MP, and deep dungeon potion automation.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. Each potion's threshold and on/off state is stored per-job, so casters and tanks can have completely different setups.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.2.5.2 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

v0.2.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After AutoPotion updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read. Type `/autopotion changelog` any time to reopen it.
- No change to potion behaviour: thresholds, per-job profiles and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.2.1 - 2026-07-02
- **Plugin icon now shows in the Dalamud installer.** The manifest (`AutoPotion.json`) had no

- No behavior changes. Part of a repo cleanup pass.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Faye, Kage
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.
- No more of that pesky 'walking' or 'finding chests'. That's for losers.
- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)
  /och … → Same as /bocchi (legacy alias; also /occultcrescenthelper)

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Valenth Siveria
metadataCompletePlugins.name: I Am Ready
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

/iar - opens the I Am Ready tool
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog: API15 finally

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Ice
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Ice's Cosmic Exploration (ICE)
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Welcome to, the dark side of, the MOOOON
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
The one-stop shop to your cosmic exploration needs! This plugin is meant to be a collective source of being able to grind out your gather and crafter relics, while also being able to help grind out the score to 500k on each class for that sleek black mech that you want ~.

- Has the ability to re-roll missions for you until you get the desired one that you want to farm
- Crafters can be fully automated with support of artisan. 
- Fisher can also be fully automated with the support of AutoHook and Navmesh
- Botanist/Miner only need Navmesh, thanks to having gathering built in directly to the plugin <3. 
- Setup what items you want to buy from the shop for cosmocredits, or spend your planetary tokens on the cosmowheel of fortune!
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
- HOPEFULLY fixed collectable issues (... man I hope)
- Added a check to see if we're gathering while fishing. (if we aren't, it'll tell autohook to start fishing. If we are in the gathering state, then we wont' do shit till we're done)
    - Hopefully this'll fix some of the bugs that I've caused... let me know if it breaks things further actually

metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Find the absolute best way to spend all your FFXIV currencies.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Fork of CurrencySpender by Blackcatz1911. Never wonder 'What should I do with this?' again. Access real-time prices from Universalis, identify missing collectibles tied to your currencies, and unlock new possibilities for utilizing your in-game resources effectively.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v1.3.1.3 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- The configuration wizard's auto-open step now sets the actual auto-open setting instead of toggling the sellables table.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.3.1.2 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- Added a map location for the Faux Commander (the Faux Hollows vendor in Idyllshire). Its Flag and TP buttons now draw like every other listed shop, and the plugin no longer logs a `Missing location: 1033921` error once at every startup.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.3.1.1 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Upstream sync through CurrencySpender 1.3.1.** New tracked currencies (Faux Leaf, Achievement Certificate, Oizys Credit, Auxesia Credit) and vendors (Quinnana, Faux Commander), data-driven custom-shop generation (in-code CustomShops replaces the hardcoded Cosmocredit item lists), upstream's config version migrations, and the Service.ObjectTable API rename.
- **New optional integrations:** Lifestream and vnavmesh IPC wrappers with upstream's MovementTask movement helpers, and the NPC/menu highlight services. All are gracefully skipped when the providing plugin is absent.
- Font rendering keeps the fork's Dalamud asset-font setup; the fork keeps its own tab UI (Windows/), teleport flow, Hub integration and Quick Controls.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.2.7.4 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- Added map locations for the two shop NPCs at the Gold Saucer that had none: the tack & feed trader at Chocobo Square and the euphoric attendant. Both now draw their Flag and TP buttons like every other listed shop instead of having no buttons at all.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Five shop NPCs remain without a location on purpose: the game's own data places them nowhere (no Level-sheet placement, no placement dataset entry - campaign and seasonal attendants such as Eirene's Rain Exchange and Ermina that only exist while their event runs). They keep the behaviour introduced in 1.2.7.3: one note at debug level, no buttons.

v1.2.7.3 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- Fixed the log being flooded with `Location not found!` errors while the spending window was open. Shops run by NPCs that have no entry in the plugin's map-location table (for example Eirene's Rain Exchange and Ermina) logged one error per row on every frame, 159,189 lines in a single session. Such a shop is now noted once at debug level, and its Flag and TP buttons are simply not drawn. Currency tracking, shop listings and the spending suggestions are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.2.7.2 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the table switches (ventures, collectables, missing collectables, items of interest, items eligible for sale, hide empty currencies), opening automatically, the minimum sales for the sellable table and the thousands separator to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: croizat, dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Lazy Fate Automation
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Fully automated FATE grinding utilizing vnavmesh, lifestream, and Gluttony Combo.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Automates FATE grinding, including Zodiac Atma, Anima Luminous Crystals, Resistance Memories, Phantom Demiatmas, Yo-kai Watch Medals, and Bicolor Gemstones. Seamlessly integrates with vnavmesh for pathing and flight, lifestream for zone swapping, TextAdvance for dialogue skipping, and Gluttony Combo/BossMod for combat. Use /lazyfate to open.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **BossMod Reborn no longer runs its own job rotations beside Gluttony Combo during FATEs.** The FATE grind creates and uses its own BossMod preset, "LazyFateAutomation", holding only the movement, FATE-targeting, level-sync and stay-close-to-target modules (melee and tanks close in, other roles hold at 10 yalms), and rewrites it each time the grind starts so an old or edited copy cannot bring job rotations back.
- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: LazyCrucible
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Crucible of the Unbroken familiar picks, filled in for every fight
metadataCompletePlugins.description: For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Fills the ten-familiar run roster at the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu and the three Battlehorn slots before every fight with the familiars that answer that fight's mechanics: elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses and crowd control, skipping knocked-out familiars and benching badly hurt ones. Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.12 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction no longer fires while AutoDuty drives the screen.** AutoDuty re-asserts its own roster through a confirm sequence that removes unfamiliar rows one per pass and holds its acceptance until they are gone; every correction written on that surface was removed before entry, and the acceptance follows the build's last pick by about half a second with nothing the plugin can observe in between — a guess there only spent the correction budget on rows that were going to be removed anyway. The surface is now left to AutoDuty entirely. The battlehorn surface is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.11 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction now waits for the roster itself to stop changing.** The previous fix judged a settled roster by edit timestamps, but the roster AutoDuty builds is driven through the monster notebook, whose selection writes never register as edits — so the timestamp stayed at screen-open while the build was still adding picks, and the correction still fired mid-build, where AutoDuty's continuing build and its confirm passes removed the added rows. The correction is now due only once the selected roster has been unchanged for 1.5 seconds — what the plugin sees every frame — never on an empty roster, and it still re-arms after any later AutoDuty write. The screen log's roster needfix line now also carries the age of the last edit (`adedit=`), the roster's quiet time (`adstb=`) and the selected count (`flutes=`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: LazyFoodBuff
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Never forget to eat your food again.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Auto-eats food in combat duties with per-job selection, auto-select based on best stats, and a low-food warning.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers auto-eating, "Only in combat duties", the minutes of food left before eating again and the low-food warning with its count to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-21)

- **"Only eat in combat duties" now covers Crucible of the Unbroken.** The five boards count as combat duties, and so does the Bentbranch Meadows entry area while playing Beastmaster (the one job that can enter), so the meal is eaten before a run starts. Eating before entry matters: a meal eaten inside does not refill HP to the raised maximum.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Optional decision diagnostics, off by default. Turn on "Log food decisions" (settings window, Advanced / Diagnostics) or run `/lazyfoodbuff telemetry on`, and every time the plugin settles on a food for the current job it writes one line to the plugin log: the food it picked, its score, and the runner-ups it beat — plus a second line when that food is actually eaten. The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

- Honest caveat: this is a data-collection investment, not an answer. The outcome side (what a food actually did to damage) needs weeks of encounter data before it says anything statistically — the plugin log will quietly accumulate the decision half in the meantime.
- Nothing about food selection changed. When the toggle is off, the only cost is one boolean read.

v0.1.3.1 (2026-09-05)

- The "What's new" popup now opens after this very update. 0.1.3.0 stayed silent the first time it ran because it had no record of the last version shown; the gate now tells an updated plugin (settings file already present) apart from a brand-new install (none yet) and only the latter stays quiet (`ChangelogGate.Options.ExistingInstall`, read from `pi.ConfigFile.Exists`.

- Nothing else changed. The notes can be reopened later with `/lazyfoodbuff changelog`.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- In-game "What's new" popup. After every update, the first time the character is logged in and out of combat, LazyFoodBuff opens a window with the release notes for every version since the last one shown. It appears once per update; pressing "Got it" (or closing it) keeps it quiet until the next update.
- `/lazyfoodbuff changelog` (or `whatsnew`) reopens the release notes at any time.
- "Open changelog on GitHub" button in the popup links to the full CHANGELOG for this plugin.

- This is the pilot of a standing rule for every lalalazy plugin: the popup code is shared across plugins and each plugin embeds its own release notes at build time. New config field `Configuration.LastSeenChangelogVersion`; on the first build carrying the feature it records the running version silently and does not open.
- The popup never opens during combat, inside a duty, while zoning, or in a cutscene - it waits until the character is free.
- `/lazyfoodbuff` with no argument still opens these settings.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: LazyRetainerLive
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.0.2 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

metadataCompletePlugins.name: LeveHelper
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: A little helper for Levequests.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: A little helper to check which Levequests have been completed and which are missing.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
- Added: You can now click on the group header in the Type filter to filter for either all Fieldcraft, Tradecraft or Grand Company Leves.
- Added: When GatherBuddy is installed, the Queue and Recipe Tree now display GatherBuddys tooltip on fish and spearfish, including info about the Bait, Time and Weather restrictions and the next uptimes.  
  - Please note that GatherBuddy uses the client language, not Dalamuds UI language like LeveHelper. It's out of my control.
- Fixed: Some gatherables did not show up in the Queue.

Regarding the Levemete filter

The game's database doesn't list which Levemete issues which Levequests and multiple old NPCs also rotate their Levequests when you complete one.

I used to scrape a wiki to gather this data, but two weeks ago, we added Levequest issuer tracking to the Tracky plugin and already have more entries than the wiki provided!

Some entries that I could confirm through another wiki are still missing, so manually added those back in for now.

If you'd like to help us, please install the Tracky plugin and enable uploads in its settings.

Thank you! :)

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Aida Enna
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Macro Chain Redux
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: A modified fork of the old Macro Chain that allows you to run multiple macros one after the other (or repeat them).
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Allows for a macro to continue onto the next macro by using '/nextmacro' on the last line of a macro.
Adding '/nextmacro' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #02
Adding '/nextmacro down' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #11
Also allows executing any macro from chat using '/runmacro'
You can repeat a macro by using /runmacro inside the macro followed by the number of the macro you're editing
Using '/macrocancel' will stop the currently running macro
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog: - Updated for patch 7.5

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Akari
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Mahjong Advisor
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog: v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.
